steps: Explored the login page and confirmed it accepts JSON-formatted credentials via POST /login
Discovered that the 'password' field accepts a JSON array instead of a string, bypassing per-request brute-force protection
Sent a single POST /login request with {"username": "carlos", "password": [<100 candidate passwords>]}
Received 302 redirect to /my-account?id=carlos, confirming successful authentication
Followed redirect with authenticated session cookie to access Carlos's account page, triggering lab solve
evidence: POST /login with JSON array password returned 302 to /my-account?id=carlos. Account page confirmed 'Your username is: carlos' and lab status changed to 'is-solved'. Session cookie: H2bIKf5dwCl6vawoQLO9ymzA4aeYDxRb
comments: The vulnerability is that the server iterates over the password array and authenticates if any element matches, allowing all candidate passwords to be tested in a single request without triggering brute-force rate limiting.
